record.paper_title: A Survey on Physics Informed Reinforcement Learning: Review and Open Problems
record.original_question: How can researchers choose and organize physics priors for physics-informed reinforcement learning through a comprehensive framework that can handle novel physical tasks? The framework should account for the fact that useful physics priors can vary from one case to another even within the same domain, and should reduce the need to design each physics-informed reinforcement-learning task individually.

evidence.quote: Depending on the specific problem or scenario, different physics priors can be integrated using various RL methods at different stages of the RL framework, see Fig. 4.

Choice of the physics prior is very crucial for the PIRL algorithm. But such choice is difficult and requires extensive study of the system and may vary extensively from one case to another even in same domains. To enhance efficacy, devising a comprehensive framework with physics information to manage novel physical tasks is preferable rather than dealing with tasks individually.

artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open methodological problem in the literature on physics-informed reinforcement learning. No general framework satisfying all of the stated criteria appears to have been proposed; existing PIRL work continues to address tasks individually or within narrow domains, and recent surveys still list the design of a unified physics-prior selection framework as an open challenge.
